children: House Speaker
Mike Johnson
(R-La.) said the Iran conflict now needs to be "brought to a resolution," while acknowledging that disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz are driving up U.S. fuel and grocery prices.
Johnson Calls For Iran War Resolution

"It’s been a priority and an objective of every administration, for 50 years nearly, to ensure that Iran didn’t have a nuclear capability. Now that’s done. Operation Epic Fury was an epic success," Johnson said in a local television interview on Wednesday. "But now we’ve got to bring that to a resolution."
Johnson did not call for an immediate end to the war or outline specific steps to wind it down. Reuters reported that Iowa Senate candidate
Ashley Hinson
and Michigan candidate
Mike Rogers
also called this week for a swift end to the conflict while proposing measures such as suspending gasoline taxes and limiting diesel exports.
Fuel Costs Deepen Pressure On Households

Johnson tied the conflict directly to household costs. "The Strait of Hormuz not being open affects commerce. It directly affects gas prices and fuel prices. And also, you know, the price of groceries, for example, because they got to be transported, and the higher fuel prices are a factor in that as well," he said.

EIA data show petroleum shipments through Hormuz averaged 4.9 million barrels per day in the second quarter, down from 21.6 million in the fourth quarter of 2025. The agency calls Hormuz one of the world’s most important oil chokepoints.
A separate Associated Press report this week found growing voter frustration over gasoline prices around $4.50 nationally, including among some Trump supporters.
Republicans Push Relief As Prices Rise
Johnson said he expects prices to ease if the waterway reopens. "I think as soon as the Strait of Hormuz is reopened … then the president’s right. Gas prices come back down."
